title: Grain Accounting Manual: Striking the Bushels Still Owed on a Grain Marketing Contract
content:
The bushels still owed on a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts are the bushels the contract commits less the bushels credited to it, struck in whole bushels, a part bushel taken to the nearest whole bushel and a half bushel taken upward, and never below zero.

## What credits the contract

1. **A load the member directed to the contract at the scale and received at the facility the contract calls for** credits the net bushels written on its scale ticket.
2. **A load the member directed to the contract at the scale but received at any other facility** credits the net bushels written on its ticket in the same way.
3. **A load the member ran straight through to the buyer** credits its net bushels at the straight-through factor, which is 0.975.
4. **Bushels the member has moved out of store onto their marketing business** are credited as well, taken from every load-out recorded on the member's storage account in the twelve months before the balance is struck, less the handling shrink taken on transferred bushels at the standard transfer rate of 1.25 percent.

## How the credit is assembled

The credited bushels are the home-facility net bushels, the credit allowed on loads received elsewhere, the straight-through credit and the transferred-bushel credit added together, and the handling shrink taken on conditioned loads is then subtracted from that total before the balance is struck against the committed bushels. No handling shrink is taken on conditioned loads.

Each component is worked to two decimal places as it is formed; the balance itself is struck in whole bushels at the end, a part bushel taken to the nearest whole bushel and a half bushel taken upward, and is never carried below zero.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical contract commits 12,000 bushels. Its tickets carry 6,000 net bushels that the member directed to the contract at the scale and that were received at the facility the contract calls for, and 1,000 net bushels that the member directed to the contract at the scale but that were received at another facility. Two loads were run straight through to the buyer, carrying 2,000 net bushels together. The member's storage account shows 800 bushels of load-outs in the twelve months before the balance is struck.

| Component | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Home-facility net bushels | 6,000.00 |
| Credit allowed on loads received elsewhere | 1,000.00 |
| Straight-through credit, being 2,000.00 taken at 0.975 | 1,950.00 |
| Transferred-bushel credit, being 800.00 less 1.25 percent | 790.00 |
| Handling shrink on conditioned loads | nil |
| **Credited bushels** | **9,740.00** |

The bushels still owed are the 12,000 committed less those 9,740 credited, being 2,260 bushels. Had the credited bushels come to 9,739.50, the balance would be 2,260.50 before the striking and 2,261 after it, the half bushel being taken upward.
